findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in controllers, so fallbacks fail in mailers/background jobs
findings.body: The accelerator's `translate` only lazy-loads the active locale (`load_locale(config.locale)` on line 68); it never loads the fallback locales returned by `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`. The only place that force-loads the fallback chain is `ApplicationController#set_locale` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 → `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`). Any translation performed outside an HTTP request — ActionMailer, Sidekiq/background workers, rake tasks, console — never runs `set_locale`, so `:en` (and the site default) yml is not loaded. When a key is missing in the user's locale the Fallbacks backend tries `:en`, finds no loaded data, and the caller gets a "translation missing" string instead of the English fallback. This defeats the stated 'server-side fallbacks' goal for exactly the server-side paths (emails etc.) that need it most. The fallback locales should be loaded inside the translate/locale-loading path rather than only from the controller.

findings.title: Fallback chain does a DB-backed SiteSetting lookup on every translation
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds its result from `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is a runtime site setting rather than a boot-time constant. `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for essentially every `I18n.t` lookup (the accelerator routes all translation through the backend), so this now performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read (and allocates a fresh array) on the hot translation path for every request. In addition to the overhead, it makes translation depend on `SiteSetting` being initialized: in contexts without a ready DB/settings (boot, `rake db:migrate`, `rake assets:precompile`, or if the setting is nil so `.to_sym` raises NoMethodError) any `I18n.t` call can raise instead of returning a translation. The fallback list should be computed once/memoized with a safe hard-coded default instead of reading SiteSetting per lookup.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
findings.body: This PR changes global i18n behavior (enables Fallbacks in every environment, replaces the default fallbacks object, and adds an `ensure_loaded!` hook) but adds no specs. There is no coverage that a key missing in a non-English locale resolves to the site default and then to English, that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locales' yml, or that a missing key still raises/returns the expected result. Given this touches translation resolution for all requests and is easy to regress, at least a request spec exercising a missing translation in a non-English locale and a unit test for `FallbackLocaleList#[]`/`ensure_loaded!` should be added.

findings.title: Translation cache key omits fallback/default locale, so changing default_locale yields stale fallback text
findings.body: The LRU cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, which only captures the requested locale. With fallbacks now resolving through `SiteSetting.default_locale`, the *value* stored for a given locale can change when an admin changes the default locale, but the key does not, so previously cached fallback-resolved strings keep being served until `I18n.reload!` happens to be called. For locales whose own translations are incomplete, this means users continue to see text from the old default-locale fallback after the setting is changed. The cache key (or a `reload!` on default_locale change) should account for the fallback chain.
